# PaCoRe: Learning to Scale Test-Time Compute with Parallel Coordinated Reasoning

- **Authors**: Jingcheng Hu, Yinmin Zhang, Shijie Shang, Xiaobo Yang, Yue Peng, Zhewei Huang, Hebin Zhou, Xin Wu, Jie Cheng, Fanqi Wan, Xiangwen Kong, Chengyuan Yao, Kaiwen Yan, Ailin Huang, Hongyu Zhou, Qi Han, Zheng Ge, Xiangyu Zhang, Heung-Yeung Shum

## In one line

PaCoRe (Parallel Coordinated Reasoning) decouples test-time compute scaling from a fixed context window by running rounds of massively parallel reasoning trajectories, compacting each trajectory's conclusion into a short message, and RL-training the model to synthesize (not just vote on) these messages into better subsequent exploration -- letting an 8B model reach 94.5% on HMMT 2025 by scaling effective test-time compute to ~2 million tokens, surpassing GPT-5's 93.2%.

## Problem

Standard sequential chain-of-thought reasoning packs every intermediate state into a single expanding context, so once the context window fills, reasoning must stop, placing a hard ceiling on how much search-driven test-time compute (TTC) can be expressed regardless of how much compute is actually available; naive parallel alternatives (majority voting, random selection among parallel attempts) also fail to fully exploit parallel exploration because models exhibit 'Reasoning Solipsism' -- ignoring rich context from other parallel branches and re-solving a problem from scratch rather than synthesizing across them, especially on problems without a simple, easily-comparable answer (e.g. code, proofs).

## Contributions

- PaCoRe, a general framework decoupling reasoning volume (effective test-time compute) from fixed model context by coordinating parallel reasoning trajectories through iterative message compaction, enabling multi-million-token effective TTC within a standard context window
- identification of 'Reasoning Solipsism' -- models ignoring rich parallel context and re-solving problems from scratch on tasks without simple comparable answers -- and a large-scale, outcome-based RL training procedure specifically curated (via two-stage filtering that excludes instances solvable by naive aggregation) to induce genuine Reasoning Synthesis rather than majority voting or random selection
- empirical results showing an 8B model trained with PaCoRe surpasses GPT-5 and several larger frontier open models on HMMT 2025 and other math/code/agentic benchmarks, with ablations isolating parallel scaling and message passing as both individually necessary for the observed scaling behavior
- public release of model checkpoints, curated training data, and inference pipeline, with the training data itself shown to be a broadly useful RLVR resource beyond the PaCoRe framework

## Method

PaCoRe executes R rounds of coordinated reasoning: each round takes the problem plus a compact message set inherited from the previous round, generates K parallel reasoning trajectories from this combined context, then compacts each trajectory's full chain down to only its final conclusion segment (discarding intermediate derivation) to form the next round's message set -- keeping per-round input length bounded even as the aggregate token count (effective TTC) across all rounds and trajectories scales into the millions. The final round degenerates to a single trajectory (K_R=1), whose compacted message is the system's answer. To train the model's synthesis capability -- critically evaluating diverse parallel perspectives, reconciling conflicting evidence, and generating a solution surpassing any individual input, rather than merely voting or aggregating -- the synthesis stage is framed as an episodic RL environment (PPO with GAE, strict on-policy, ORZ setup) where the policy receives a problem x and a message set M (drawn from a cached pool generated by an initial RLVR-trained checkpoint) and is rewarded on the correctness of its synthesized trajectory. Training data is deliberately curated in two stages to force genuine synthesis rather than shortcuts: Stage 1 filters for scenarios where naive aggregation fails (low mean accuracy across the message set, i.e. most inputs are individually wrong), and Stage 2 further restricts to instances with intermediate synthesis accuracy (0 < synthesis_acc < 1) using an intermediate checkpoint -- ensuring the model cannot succeed via majority voting or random selection, since the pool it draws from is mostly incorrect. PaCoRe-8B is initialized from an internally RL-post-trained Qwen3-8B-Base checkpoint (RLVR-8B) and evaluated on AIME 2025, HMMT 2025, IMOAnswerBench, Apex, LiveCodeBench, HLE(text), and MultiChallenge under three coordinated-reasoning configurations (Low: K=[4,]; Medium: K=[16,]; High: K=[32,4]) against frontier reasoning models (GPT-5, Qwen3-235B-Thinking, GLM-4.6, DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus, Kimi-K2-Thinking) and against a Self-Consistency (majority-vote) baseline at matched or larger sampling budgets.

## Results

PaCoRe-8B consistently outperforms its own starting checkpoint (RLVR-8B) on every benchmark and setting, and even in the Low setting achieves 88.1% on HMMT 2025 and 75.8% on LiveCodeBench, already surpassing considerably larger models such as Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 and DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus. In the High setting, PaCoRe-8B reaches 94.5% on HMMT 2025 (surpassing GPT-5's 93.2%) and 78.4% on IMOAnswerBench, by scaling effective TTC to approximately 2 million tokens per problem; on the extremely challenging Apex benchmark, RLVR-8B fails to answer any question correctly (0.0%) while PaCoRe-8B (High) achieves 2.3%, and on LiveCodeBench PaCoRe-8B reaches 78.2%, competitive with GLM-4.6 and Kimi-K2-Thinking. Ablations isolate both core design choices as necessary: parallel scaling (K=[N,]) uses TTC far more effectively than sequential scaling (K=[1,...,1]) at the same total trajectory count (Figure 4 left); and message passing (compaction) is essential for scaling -- without it, performance degrades as TTC scales and is fundamentally capped by context length, whereas full PaCoRe with compaction scales robustly and unboundedly (Figure 4 right, showing 'W/O Message Passing' input tokens exceeding the model's context limit as trajectories increase, while 'W Message Passing' stays flat). Training-dynamics tracking (Figure 5) shows the frequency of cross-checking linguistic markers ('reference', 'ref <number>') rises steadily across training in both math and code domains, and near-zero initial frequency specifically in the code domain aligns with untrained models' poor test-time scaling on LiveCodeBench (Figure 1 right) -- direct evidence training is what induces the coordinated-reasoner behavior. The Emergent Correctness Rate (probability of a correct synthesized solution given an all-wrong input message set) rises over training in both domains, up to ~10% for math and ~4% for code by step 600-700, demonstrating the model learns to reconstruct valid solutions from entirely erroneous partial evidence -- something majority voting or random selection cannot do by construction. Compared head-to-head against Self-Consistency (matched or larger sampling budgets, up to @256 for RLVR-8B and PaCoRe-8B-as-SC), PaCoRe's coordinated reasoning shows more consistent, non-saturating improvement, while the Self-Consistency baseline saturates rapidly (e.g. RLVR-8B SC plateaus around 89-90% on AIME2025 from @64 to @256, while PaCoRe High reaches 93.7% using fewer total tokens in some comparisons). PaCoRe generalizes beyond math/code: on SWE-Verified (software engineering, via Agentless), PaCoRe-8B (low) reaches 34.0% resolve rate versus RLVR-8B's 29.8%, with no task-specific tuning; on MultiChallenge (multi-turn conversation), PaCoRe-8B (high) improves the RLVR-8B baseline from 33.3% to 48.0%. The curated PaCoRe training data itself transfers as a general-purpose RLVR resource: standard RLVR training on this data (only 50 iterations, minimal compute) raises a separate SFT model's AIME2025 accuracy from 81.4% to 83.2% and LiveCodeBench from 66.0% to 74.0%. A small-scale backbone study (Qwen3-1.7B) shows the same scaling pattern holds at smaller model size and surpasses a reported 1.7B baseline (AggLM) at matched budget (35.2% vs. 32.1% on HMMT2025 at K=[8,]), improving further to 41.9% under the full multi-round High configuration.

## Limitations

PaCoRe currently scales the volume of test-time compute via massive parallelism rather than strictly optimizing intelligence density (utility derived per unit of compute); the implementation employs homogeneous search without explicit division of labor among trajectories, and the authors flag designing strategies that reduce redundancy via specialized, cooperative trajectory roles as future work. The framework is validated exclusively on pure-text domains to isolate intrinsic reasoning; it has not been integrated with external tool usage or multimodal perception, and extending PaCoRe to agentic settings requiring coordinated tool interaction and multimodal inputs is identified as a critical next step. PaCoRe currently constitutes a distinct training stage within the authors' overall model pipeline, and how to co-optimize it jointly with foundational pretraining and post-training processes (e.g. via using the framework to drive synthetic data generation) has not yet been investigated.

## Why it matters here

- **overthinking**: An important counterpoint within the topic rather than a mitigation method: PaCoRe deliberately scales test-time compute far beyond what a single sequential trace could hold (millions of tokens) and shows large, apparently non-saturating accuracy gains from doing so on genuinely hard problems (HMMT, IMO-level, Apex) -- directly relevant to calibrating claims elsewhere in this archive (e.g. the FoE/RED and Revisiting Test-Time Scaling papers) that additional reasoning/exploration is typically unhelpful or actively harmful. The key reconciling factor the paper surfaces is 'Reasoning Solipsism': naive parallel exploration (more samples, majority voting) fails for exactly the reason those overthinking-skeptical papers document, but PaCoRe's explicitly-trained synthesis capability (reconciling conflicting parallel evidence rather than restarting from scratch) is what unlocks genuine benefit from more compute -- suggesting the overthinking literature's 'more thinking doesn't help' findings may be specific to naive sequential/self-revision or untrained-synthesis regimes rather than a fundamental limit on test-time compute itself.

## Abstract

We introduce Parallel Coordinated Reasoning (PaCoRe), a training-and-inference framework designed to overcome a central limitation of contemporary language models: their inability to scale test-time compute (TTC) far beyond sequential reasoning under a fixed context window. PaCoRe departs from the traditional sequential paradigm by driving TTC through massive parallel exploration coordinated via a message-passing architecture in multiple rounds. Each round launches many parallel reasoning trajectories, compacts their findings into context-bounded messages, and synthesizes these messages to guide the next round and ultimately produce the final answer. Trained end-to-end with large-scale, outcome-based reinforcement learning, the model masters the synthesis abilities required by PaCoRe and scales to multi-million-token effective TTC without exceeding context limits. The approach yields strong improvements across diverse domains and notably pushes reasoning beyond frontier systems in mathematics: an 8B model reaches 94.5% on HMMT 2025, surpassing GPT-5’s 93.2% by scaling effective TTC to roughly two million tokens. We open-source model checkpoints, training data, and the full inference pipeline to accelerate follow-up work.
